title: CCPA & California Privacy Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete CCPA compliance checklist to protect your California privacy rights. Step-by-step guide for data deletion, opt-outs, and privacy controls.
intro: The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA) give you powerful rights over your personal data. This checklist helps you exercise those rights and protect your privacy from data brokers and companies.

items.task: Learn your five key CCPA privacy rights
items.why: Understanding your rights is the first step to protecting your privacy under California law.
items.howTo: Review the right to know what data is collected, right to delete personal information, right to opt-out of data sales, right to correct inaccurate data, and right to non-discrimination for exercising rights.

items.task: Identify which businesses must comply with CCPA
items.why: Not all businesses are covered by CCPA, so knowing which ones are helps you focus your privacy efforts.
items.howTo: Look for businesses with annual revenues over $25 million, those that process data of 100,000+ consumers, or derive 50%+ revenue from selling personal information.

items.task: Understand what counts as personal information under CCPA
items.why: CCPA's definition of personal information is broader than you might think, covering browsing history, location data, and more.
items.howTo: Review the 11 categories including identifiers, commercial information, biometric data, internet activity, geolocation data, and inferences about your preferences.

items.task: Request disclosure of your personal information
items.why: Knowing what data companies have about you is essential for making informed privacy decisions.
items.howTo: Submit requests to major companies asking for categories of data collected, sources, business purposes, and third parties who received your data. Most companies have online forms or email addresses for these requests.

items.task: Request deletion of your personal information
items.why: Removing unnecessary personal data reduces your privacy risk and limits future data misuse.
items.howTo: Contact companies to delete your data unless they need it for legal compliance, fraud prevention, or completing transactions. Start with companies you no longer use.

items.task: Opt out of personal information sales
items.why: Preventing data sales stops your information from being shared with unknown third parties for profit.
items.howTo: Look for 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' links on websites, submit opt-out requests, and use the Global Privacy Control setting in Incognito Browser to automatically signal your opt-out preference.

items.task: Request correction of inaccurate personal information
items.why: Incorrect data can lead to wrong decisions about you for credit, employment, or services.
items.howTo: Contact businesses to correct inaccurate information in your profiles, especially with credit agencies, background check companies, and data brokers.

items.task: Identify major data brokers that may have your information
items.why: Data brokers collect and sell your personal information, often without your direct knowledge or consent.
items.howTo: Research major data brokers like Acxiom, LexisNexis, Spokeo, and WhitePages. Check the California Attorney General's data broker registry for a comprehensive list.

items.task: Submit opt-out requests to data brokers
items.why: Removing your information from data broker databases reduces identity theft risk and unwanted marketing.
items.howTo: Visit each data broker's website to find their opt-out process. Some require online forms, others accept email requests. Keep records of your requests and follow up if needed.

items.task: Monitor data broker compliance with your requests
items.why: Some data brokers may not fully comply or may re-add your information from other sources.
items.howTo: Check back in 30-60 days to verify your information was removed. Set calendar reminders to repeat opt-out requests periodically as new data may be added.

items.task: Enable Global Privacy Control in your browser
items.why: GPC automatically signals your opt-out preference to websites, saving time and ensuring consistent privacy choices.
items.howTo: Use Incognito Browser which has built-in Global Privacy Control, or enable GPC in browsers like Firefox and Chrome through extensions or settings.

items.task: Review privacy policies of services you use regularly
items.why: Understanding how companies handle your data helps you make informed decisions about which services to use.
items.howTo: Look for sections on data collection, sharing practices, your rights, and contact information for privacy requests. Focus on services you use most frequently.

items.task: Adjust privacy settings to limit data sharing
items.why: Proactive privacy settings prevent unnecessary data collection and sharing before it happens.
items.howTo: Review settings in social media, mobile apps, and online accounts. Turn off location tracking, ad personalization, and data sharing where possible.

items.task: Keep records of all privacy requests and responses
items.why: Documentation helps you track compliance and provides evidence if you need to file complaints.
items.howTo: Save copies of request emails, confirmation numbers, and company responses. Create a simple spreadsheet to track request dates, companies, and outcomes.
